comments.body:
## Fresh field evidence (2026-08-20) — candidate driver of machine-wide saturation

Today's session ran up to 5 concurrent agents, each repeatedly resolving attested gates
(`review-plan`, `verify-completion`, `review-code`). Observed on the host:

- sustained load average 12.02 (15-min 8.53, i.e. still climbing), 19 rebar-related processes
- at one point three processes pinned at ~95% CPU simultaneously, from a worktree unrelated
  to the work I was driving
- two subagents stalled outright, twice in a row, and the harness's own tooling began timing
  out — symptoms of resource starvation rather than agent fault

If every attested gate resolution materialises ~620 MiB / 69,984 blobs with no reuse, as this
ticket measures, then N concurrent agents running gates multiply that directly. Five agents
cycling gates is single-digit GiB of fresh file writes per round, on a key that changes every
~26 seconds so it effectively never hits.

**Stated honestly: this is a plausible contributor, not a proven cause.** I did not instrument
the snapshot store during the saturation window, and I first mis-attributed the load to another
session's test suite. What would prove it: watch `<store>/tickets-<sha>` entry creation and
bytes written while a gate runs, and correlate with the CPU spikes.

Why it matters for prioritisation: this ticket is currently framed as a write-amplification and
disk-waste problem. The multi-agent interaction makes it a **throughput** problem as well — the
cost lands on whichever machine is running the agents, and it scales with the concurrency this
project actively encourages. That argues for raising it above P2, or at least for recording the
concurrency multiplier in the ticket's framing.

Related and worth sequencing together: `moist-short-lionfish` (linear drain-gate walk on every
write) hits the same store from the write side, and `carryable-basalt-beagle` (leak-guard
fixture deleting concurrent writes under REPO_ROOT) is a third instance of the same theme —
concurrent sessions sharing one repo root with no coordination.

No description edit — evidence in comments to keep any attestation current.

comments.body:
# Phase 1 EXIT — mechanism proven at runtime (rebar-debug)

Worktree `fix-naga-snapshot` @ `origin/main`. One root cause; it explains every symptom the
ticket records. All three handed-in claims re-verified independently — two confirmed, and the
key one confirmed by *observation*, not by reading source.

## RC — `materialize_tickets` writes every blob fresh, so adjacent tickets SHAs share nothing

`materialize_tickets` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:616-724`) content-addresses the
entry as `<store>/tickets-<sha>` and builds it with `_materialize_tree` (`:373-410`), i.e.
`git read-tree` into a throwaway index + `git checkout-index --all --force --prefix=<build>/`.
`checkout-index` materializes the committed blob for **every** tree entry. There is no
hardlink, no reflink, and no delta against the neighbouring entry that differs by one file.

The key is the live tickets tip, which advances roughly every 26 s, so the `dest.is_dir()`
cache-hit branch (`:672`) is effectively never taken.

### E1 — runtime measurement (the ticket's central claim is `dynamic`; source reading would not have sufficed)

Scratch store + scratch tracker repo, 300-file tree. Five `materialize_tickets(fetch=False)`
calls, each after a commit touching **exactly one** of the 300 files — the shape of a real
tickets commit (the ticket measured the last 5 consecutive tickets commits at 1 file each).

    res#1 tip=1e150114 -> entries=1 files= 302 bytes= 1.14 MiB
    res#2 tip=d5d1d23d -> entries=2 files= 602 bytes= 2.29 MiB
    res#3 tip=eb904552 -> entries=3 files= 902 bytes= 3.43 MiB
    res#4 tip=48bade46 -> entries=4 files=1202 bytes= 4.58 MiB
    res#5 tip=934cc0a3 -> entries=5 files=1502 bytes= 5.72 MiB

    RESULT entries_created=5 for 5 resolutions
           byte_total(accounted)=5.72 MiB   real bytes on disk=5.72 MiB
           distinct inodes for an IDENTICAL unchanged file across entries: 5 (shared groups=0)

Strictly linear: **5 resolutions -> 5 entries -> 5 trees.** The decisive observation is the
last line — `ticket-0100/events.jsonl` is byte-identical in all five commits and still occupies
**five distinct inodes**. Sharing is not merely rare here; it is structurally absent.

Amplification in this fixture: 300 files rewritten per 1-file delta (300x). On the real store
(69,984 blobs) the same structure gives ~7x10^4.

**What E1 discriminates against.** It kills "the key sometimes hits" (5 entries for 5
resolutions, zero hits) and "the janitor would have reclaimed it" (this measures the
*production* side in isolation — no janitor ran). It also confirms `itchy-arbored-peccary`'s
accounting fix is live and correct here: accounted 5.72 MiB == real 5.72 MiB.

### E2 — `SnapshotHandle._cleanup` is a permanent no-op (confirmed, and it is NOT the defect)

Handed in as a claim a sibling agent had already checked; re-verified both ways.
`grep -rn "_cleanup" src/` returns exactly two sites — the field declaration
(`repo_snapshot.py:199`) and the read in `__exit__` (`:212-213`). **No producer anywhere in
`src/` assigns it.** Observed at runtime through a real `resolve_gate_handle(...)`:

    handle.source=attested sha=49d6fb2e tickets_path=set
    handle._cleanup = None
    after __exit__: cleanup invoked? False  (entry still on disk: True)

So `__exit__` is inert. **Recorded, but explicitly not the fix**: the entry is a *cache*, and
per-review release would defeat caching outright rather than repair it. The defect is that the
cache has no reuse, not that it is never released. Disposition below.

## Field state on this host

64,483 live entries (35,033 `tickets-*`, 29,450 code), consistent with the ticket's
"64,000+ / 47.2 GiB". Nothing was hand-deleted — other sessions are running gates against this
store continuously.

## Defect legitimacy — `defect`

`docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md` D2 grounds the whole layout on "An immutable SHA
is a perfect cache key", and `src/rebar/_snapshot/cache.py:154` restates the operative
assumption: "The same SHA is often requested by several concurrent gates." For the tickets key
that premise is false — E1 shows the same SHA is essentially *never* requested twice. D5
describes a bounded, reclaimable cache; what this key produces is an append-only log of full
copies. Behaviour diverges from a cited design invariant, not merely from an expectation.

## Attribution — `swampy-knot-mirage` (615c-7646-4566-4bb8), class `plan_defect`

**Two candidates, and the date test separates them.**

| commit | date | what it did |
|---|---|---|
| `ec85e4cd54` | 2026-06-27 | **introduced** `materialize_tickets`: `dest = store / f"tickets-{sha}"` + `_materialize_tree`, a full fresh tree per SHA. Trailer `Bug: 615c-7646-4566-4bb8`. |
| `ae6f2ac57a` | 2026-08-12 | introduced `_pin_tickets_sha`, moving the pin from the code repo's `origin/tickets` mirror to the live tracker `HEAD` (bug 2a6f — the verifier was reading a store 6757 commits stale). |

`ae6f2ac57a` is the tempting answer: it is recent, it sits in the function I am editing, and it
lands just before the 2026-08-17 saturation window. **It is the wrong answer.** It changed
*where the pin is read from*, not the copy structure — and on the dominant `fetch=True` path
the pre-existing code already called `resolve_ref("origin/tickets", fetch=True)`, which fetches
and resolves the **live shared tip**. Key velocity was already ~26 s before it. Blaming it would
charge a correctness fix for reading a stale store with a write-amplification defect it did not
introduce.

The mechanism has been present unchanged since 2026-06-27 and predates the incident by seven
weeks; it grew acute only because the tickets tree grew to ~620 MiB. A latent design defect that
became expensive is still attributed to the design.

**Divergence from the blame default, recorded explicitly:** a whole-file `git blame` majority on
`repo_snapshot.py` would name recent editors, and a blame of the `materialize_tickets` body
would surface `ae6f2ac57a`. Neither is the origin. `ec85e4cd54` added a **second populate path**
into a store whose content-addressed contract (ADR 0005 D2) was already on the page in front of
its reviewer, without asking whether the new key domain had the reuse that contract assumes.
The consumer is the culprit; ADR 0005's own epic could not have known about a future producer.

This is the **same origin** `itchy-arbored-peccary` independently attributed for its RC-2, by the
same reasoning — arrived at here from a different mechanism, which corroborates rather than
copies it. Class `plan_defect`: 615c's plan scoped "materialize a SEPARATE, read-only, pinned
copy of the ticket store" and the flaw is in that plan, not in a later regression.

## Not absorbed (checked, per the brief)

- `undamaged-epidermic-kakarikis` — janitor only starts in the review-bot process. Untouched:
  this fix is production-side and reclaims nothing.
- `famous-digital-dingo` — no mtime bump on a cache hit. Untouched: E1 shows the hit branch is
  essentially never reached, which is precisely what this fix changes the economics of, but the
  missing `touch_entry` call is still absent afterwards.

No description edit — evidence in comments to keep any attestation current.

# Phase 2 COMPLETE — fix pushed as Gerrit change 1980

Commit `c9c9a41591`, branch `fix-naga-snapshot` off `origin/main`.
https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1980

## Fix

**AC-1 — a review no longer writes a full copy.** New `src/rebar/_snapshot/delta_tree.py`
(301 LOC): pick the newest published `tickets-<sha2>` entry whose commit this clone can read,
hardlink the paths the two trees share, and let `git checkout-index --force -z --stdin` rewrite
only the paths that differ. `materialize_tickets` gains ~10 lines of wiring; the pre-existing
`_materialize_tree` call is now the fail-closed fallback and is otherwise untouched.

Approach chosen against ADR 0005's integrity guarantee, as the AC asks. The two rejected
alternatives are rejected for cause, not preference:

* *Pin a coarser/stabler key* would re-open bug 2a6f — `ae6f2ac57a` moved the pin to the live
  tracker HEAD precisely because a staler pin made the verifier report recorded comments as
  nonexistent. Trading freshness for size would regress a fixed bug.
* *Materialize only the paths the gate reads* is not knowable ahead of time: the agent may
  `show_ticket` any ticket in the store.

Hardlinking changes only **storage**, never contents — `tickets-<sha>` still holds exactly the
tree at `<sha>` — so the attestation basis is untouched. That is asserted, not assumed: the
oracle checks every entry's path set against `git ls-tree -r` and every file's bytes against
`git show`.

**AC-3 — byte accounting.** Already satisfied by `itchy-arbored-peccary` and deliberately not
re-implemented. It did need a correction to stay *true*: `entry_size` summed `st_size` per file
with no inode awareness, so shared blobs would have been counted once per referencing entry and
inflated `byte_total` by a factor of k. It now charges `st_size // st_nlink`, which sums back to
the true on-disk size across the k links, leaves unshared files (`st_nlink == 1`, i.e. every
code entry) completely unaffected, and is self-correcting under eviction.

**AC-4 — docs.** ADR 0005 D2 now states the key-reuse assumption explicitly ("an immutable key
is not automatically a good one") and records how each entry kind satisfies it — code entries by
*key* reuse, ticket entries by *content* reuse. `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` gains the
operator-facing version.

## AC-2 — RED -> GREEN, held out, with teeth

The oracle was authored before any fix existed, confirmed RED for the right reason, then moved
**out of the worktree entirely** (not merely omitted from the prompt) with `tests/` declared
off-limits to the implementing subagent. It asserts the algorithmic property — distinct-inode
bytes per resolution — never wall-clock.

    RED   4 adjacent-SHA resolutions consumed 3200027 bytes; one tree is ~800000   (4.00x)
    GREEN 1 passed

**Mutation 1** — disable the donor path, re-introducing the confirmed mechanism: RED again at
*exactly* 3200027 bytes. Restored: GREEN.

**Mutation 2, and why it exists.** Reviewing my own oracle I found it could not catch the
failure mode that mattered most. An implementation that enumerated donor contents by *walking
the donor directory* instead of by `git ls-tree` passes every assertion on a clean fixture — and
in production would either copy untracked files into an entry whose tree does not contain them,
or (with a count-based completeness check) fall back on every single call, leaving the fix
permanently inert while CI stayed green. An independent write-safety audit had just measured
**4,844 `.cache.json` files inside one live entry**, so this is the normal state of a donor, not
an edge case.

So `test_donor_untracked_files_do_not_leak_into_a_new_entry` seeds a donor with exactly those
artefacts. Against the walk-based implementation it fails on
`tickets/..cache.json.abc.tmp` leaking into the new entry; against the shipped one it passes.

**Refactoring litmus.** Every assertion is on observable on-disk output — distinct-inode bytes,
inode identity, path sets vs `git ls-tree`, contents vs `git show`. No private name, no
intermediate variable, no source grep. Demonstrated rather than claimed: a `ruff format` pass
(behaviour-preserving) kept it green while the behavioural mutation still turned it red.

One defect of my own surfaced during validation — an unused local that tripped `make lint`. It
changes no assertion, and both the suite and mutation 2 were re-run after removing it.

## Two safety findings that changed the design

Both came from the independent audit, and both would have been silent failures:

1. **Donor contents != donor tree** (above). Corrected mid-implementation.
2. **`.ticket-write.lock` is a *tracked* file**, so it is materialized into every entry — and
   `fcntl.flock` is scoped to the **inode**. Hardlinking it would make a lock taken through
   entry A block a writer in entry B, invisibly, until it deadlocked. It is now forced into the
   rewrite set and never shared.

Symlinks and gitlinks also fail closed (`os.link` would dereference a symlink; a gitlink has no
blob), as do an absent-objects clone, an incomplete donor, a cross-device or hardlink-less
filesystem, and a delta no smaller than the tree.

## Gates

`make lint` PASS - `make typecheck` PASS (614 files) - complexity `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`
(no baseline edit) - **full unit sweep 11,939 passed, 44 skipped** - targeted snapshot/gate
suites 116 passed - `check_raw_git_writes`, `check_wall_clock_asserts`, `check_comment_hygiene`,
`check_config_reads`, `check_config_ownership`, `check_server_manifest`,
`check_verify_gate_parity`, `check_adr_numbers`, `check_docs_index` all PASS.
Module sizes: `repo_snapshot.py` 739, `delta_tree.py` 301 — both inside the 800 cap, and the new
module is well clear of the 100-LOC floor.

## Scope

Nothing hand-deleted from the live store, as instructed. Neither sibling ticket was absorbed:
`undamaged-epidermic-kakarikis` (janitor starts only in the review-bot process) and
`famous-digital-dingo` (no mtime bump on a cache hit) both survive this change untouched — this
is production-side only, it reclaims nothing and adds no `touch_entry`.

Three tickets filed and linked `discovered_from`: `atrophied-exact-indianabat` (entries are not
actually immutable; this already breaks the reverify TOFU digest), `adroit-degraded-gourami`
(the code-entry path has the identical construct — measured at 4.00x — held out because code
snapshots are the attestation basis for signed verdicts and deserve their own review), and
`subtle-brinish-fugu` (the dead `_cleanup` field).

No description edit — evidence in comments to keep any attestation current.

## Patchset 2 on Gerrit 1980 — answering the `LLM-Review -1`

Took over the change from a prior session. Patchset 2 pushed; PS1's `LLM-Review -1` and
`Verified +1` were cleared by the upload, as expected.

### Finding 3 (`bugfix-size-attestation`) — already stale when it was reported, no restructuring

The reviewer blocked on "376 non-test lines, over the 150-line floor … verdict: unsigned; no
plan-review attestation record". Verified the line count independently against the Gerrit PS1
file list (9 + 25 + 301 + 17 + 24 = 376). The attestation claim was true at vote time and is
not true now:

| event | time (UTC) |
| --- | --- |
| review bot cast `LLM-Review -1` | 2026-08-21 07:27:53 |
| plan-review attestation `signed_at` | 2026-08-21 07:43:42 |

The attestation was signed **15m49s after** the vote. `rebar review-plan 8386-a512-4815-4e6b
--status` returns `{"ok": true, "verdict": "certified", "currency_basis": "file_impact"}` —
re-checked after all of the patchset-2 edits, from inside the worktree, and it did **not** flip
to `stale-code`. So the change was NOT decomposed to duck the line floor: a fix whose size is
legitimately authorised by a signed plan should not be carved up to satisfy a check that has
since been satisfied.

### Findings 1 and 2 — one cause: the declared janitor work was missing from PS1

Confirmed the parent diagnosis against the Gerrit file list. PS1 touched `cache.py`,
`delta_tree.py`, `repo_snapshot.py`, two docs and `tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py` — but
neither `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py` nor `tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py`, both of
which this ticket's own reviewed `file_impact` declares (`_evict credits bytes actually freed;
startup_sweep dedupes inodes` / `RED->GREEN oracle for shared-entry eviction accounting`). So
PS1 changed `entry_size` to charge `st_size // max(1, st_nlink)` and left every consumer of
that figure alone. This is `incomplete-implementation`, not a design error, and finishing it is
**inside** the authorised scope of the bug fix rather than a widening of it.

### What changed

The fix is to stop asking one function three different questions:

* `entry_size` — plain `st_size`. REPORTING only; it deliberately double-counts a shared blob.
  Reverted to its pre-change behaviour and kept as the subsystem's exported size primitive.
* `exclusive_size` — files with `st_nlink == 1`. The increment for **both** ends of the running
  total: populating adds exactly the bytes whose first link it created, evicting frees exactly
  the bytes whose last link it removes. Each inode is added once and subtracted once, so the
  incremental total tracks the authoritative walk with no drift and no rounding.
* `distinct_bytes` — each inode once. Ground truth for `startup_sweep`.

`_evict` now measures with `exclusive_size` before the rename-to-trash, so `free += reclaimed`
in the watermark loop credits bytes that actually left the disk; `startup_sweep` reconciles to
`distinct_bytes`; `materialize_tickets` and `cache.acquire` credit `exclusive_size` on populate.

The apportioned `st_size // st_nlink` is rejected and the ADR records why: it divides bytes
fairly for a report, but as an increment it credits a 1/k share of bytes still on disk, so the
free-space loop stops short of its watermark. Measured on the new fixture: evicting one of
three sharing entries credited **69,997 bytes while freeing 20,000**. Left uncorrected that
makes the original disk-exhaustion symptom worse, not better — the pass believes it recovered
space it did not.

Eviction policy, watermark semantics and the tunables are untouched.

### Both advisories closed

* `.ticket-write.lock` unshareable-inode contract
  (`test_write_lock_never_shares_an_inode_between_entries`): pinned **behaviourally** — a
  `flock` held through entry A must not block a non-blocking `flock` in entry B — plus the
  structural inode-distinctness assert, plus a guard that an ordinary unchanged blob IS shared,
  so the test cannot pass vacuously on a tree where the delta path never fired.
* `st_nlink > 1` accounting (`test_the_three_size_questions_on_a_known_inode_layout`): a
  hand-built layout with two links to one 1000-byte inode; every expectation is a literal read
  off the layout, nothing derived from the code under test.

### Non-tautological oracles + kill matrix

The janitor accounting tests measure the store with a per-inode walk written **separately** from
`cache.distinct_bytes` (documented as deliberate at the helper), so both sides of each assertion
can disagree — an accounting test that computes its expectation via the function under test
proves only that the code agrees with itself. Eight mutations, each on an independent side:

| # | mutation | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | `exclusive_size` -> `st_size // nlink` (the rejected apportionment) | KILLED |
| M2 | `exclusive_size` -> plain `st_size` (sharing ignored) | KILLED |
| M3 | `distinct_bytes` -> no inode dedupe | KILLED |
| M4 | `entry_size` -> `st_size // nlink` (the PS1 behaviour) | KILLED |
| M5 | `_evict` credits `entry_size` (pre-fix janitor) | KILLED |
| M6 | `startup_sweep` sums `entry_size` (pre-fix sweep) | KILLED |
| M7 | populate credits `entry_size` (pre-fix accounting) | KILLED |
| M8 | `delta_tree` drops `writes \| _unshareable(target_paths)` | KILLED (twice, independently) |

**M7 initially SURVIVED.** Every existing accounting test began with `startup_sweep`, whose
authoritative walk laundered any over-credit made at populate time — the two independent sides
were moving in step. Added
`test_populating_shared_entries_tracks_real_disk_without_a_sweep`, which never sweeps, and
which also asserts `sum(entry_size) > on_disk` so the equality it checks is discriminating
rather than satisfiable by any accounting. M7 then died. No survivors, no equivalent-mutant
claims.

M8 was checked twice: once whole (the structural inode assert fires), and once with the
structural assert disabled, to prove the `flock` leg kills on its own rather than riding along.

### Gates

`make lint` (incl. the shrink-only complexity ratchet: `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`),
`make typecheck` (614 files clean), full unit sweep **11944 passed, 44 skipped**. Largest
`src/rebar/_snapshot` module is 739 LOC, under the 800 cap.

Not closing the ticket: patchset 2 is awaiting `LLM-Review` and `Verified`.

## Discovered from

rebar-debug on bug `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` (3a52-2d79-320d-4fed), root cause RC-A. See
that ticket's "Phase 1 EXIT" comment for the full evidence trail.

## Problem

`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:99` calls `materialize_tickets(...)` on every attested gate
resolution. `materialize_tickets` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:675-703`)
content-addresses the entry as `<store>/tickets-<sha>` and builds it with `_materialize_tree`
(`:373-410`, `git read-tree` + `git checkout-index`) — every file written fresh, with no
hardlinking, no delta against a neighbouring entry, and no per-review release
(`SnapshotHandle._cleanup` at `:199` is never assigned by any producer).

The key is the live tickets-branch tip: `_pin_tickets_sha` (`:534-609`) resolves the tracker
via `config.tracker_dir()`, and `tracker_dir_override()` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:65-79`)
returns `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` verbatim.

Measured on `origin/tickets`:

- **69,984 blobs**, ≈620 MiB (~800 MiB allocated). The code snapshot alongside it is
  41.6 MiB / 3,131 files — **15x smaller**.
- **1,374 commits** in a 10-hour window (2026-08-17 18:00 → 2026-08-18 04:00 PDT): the tip
  moves every ~26 seconds.
- each of the last 5 consecutive tickets commits changed **exactly 1 file**.

So a one-file delta produces a fresh 620 MiB copy — roughly 10^5x write amplification — on a
key with effectively **zero reuse**. The review-bot's own `code_review` artifact write
(`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`, `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:120`) guarantees the ref advances
between reviews even if nothing else in the fleet were writing.

On the review-bot host this modelled 2.5-10 GiB/h of root-disk growth; the measured rate during
the 2026-08-17 incident was 4.4 GiB/h.

## Why this is a defect

`docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md` D2 rests on "an immutable SHA is a perfect cache
key", which holds only for keys with **reuse**. This key has none, so the structure behaves as
an append-only log of full copies rather than the bounded, reclaimable cache the ADR describes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A review no longer writes a full copy of the ticket tree when the previous entry differs
      by a handful of files (hardlink/reflink against the prior entry, materialize only the
      paths the gate actually reads, or pin a coarser/stabler key) — with the chosen approach
      justified against ADR 0005's integrity guarantees.
- [ ] A test observes the amplification RED (N reviews across N adjacent tickets SHAs consume
      ~1 tree, not N trees) and GREEN after the repair.
- [ ] `materialize_tickets` participates in the store's byte accounting (see the sibling
      ticket) so the entries it creates are visible to any size-based reclaim.
- [ ] ADR 0005 / `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` updated to state the key-reuse assumption and how
      the tickets key satisfies it.

_evict credits bytes actually freed; startup_sweep dedupes inodes
RED->GREEN oracle for blob reuse + donor untracked-file guard
RED->GREEN oracle for shared-entry eviction accounting
